seoTitle: Washoe County School District Calendar: WCSD Dates & PDFs
seoDescription: Reviewed WCSD Balanced calendar dates, official PDFs, breaks, contingency-day rules, and separate Gerlach, Incline, and TMCC calendar guidance.
districtFact: WCSD covers 6,316 square miles of northern Nevada, from Gerlach near the Black Rock Desert to Incline Village at Lake Tahoe. That geography is reflected in its calendar system: most students use the Balanced Calendar, while Gerlach, Incline, and TMCC publish separate schedules.

about.title: One District, Four Calendar Tracks
about.content: The Balanced Calendar is the districtwide reference used on this page, but it is not universal. WCSD also publishes separate Gerlach, Incline, and TMCC calendars. Those schedules can change opening dates, local breaks, college-alignment dates, grading periods, contingency days, and the final day of school.

about.title: From Reno-Sparks to Tahoe and the Black Rock Desert
about.content: WCSD reports 59,565 students across 6,316 square miles. The district reaches from its Reno-Sparks population center to Incline Village at Lake Tahoe and Gerlach near the Black Rock Desert, so the calendar choice is tied to a student's school rather than simply to a Washoe County address.

about.title: Contingency Days Need Year-Specific Reading
about.content: WCSD does not use the contingency label the same way in every reviewed year. The 2025-26 Balanced Calendar places contingency dates after the last scheduled student day, while the 2026-27 and 2027-28 Balanced Calendars mark their final contingency dates as days in session leading to the last day of school.

about.title: Professional Development Can Count as a School Day
about.content: Several WCSD professional-development dates are non-student days but are counted as school days in session under the Nevada Administrative Code note printed on the official PDFs. Families should treat them as no-school days for students without subtracting them from WCSD's published 180-day total.

calendarNotes: This district page uses WCSD's Balanced Calendar as its primary reference. Before saving dates, confirm whether the student's school follows the Balanced, Gerlach, Incline, or TMCC schedule because opening dates, breaks, and last days can differ.

planningTips.title: Planning with the WCSD Calendar
content: Confirm the assigned school's calendar track before booking travel; Gerlach, Incline, and TMCC do not simply mirror the Balanced Calendar.
Read contingency-day notes for the specific year. In 2026-27 and 2027-28, the dates printed as contingency days in session are part of the final scheduled attendance window.
Treat professional-development dates as student non-attendance days even when the PDF counts them as school days in session under Nevada rules.
Conference-week dates are academic planning markers, not automatically a full week of closures; ask the school for its conference schedule and dismissal details.
For TMCC High School, use the separate calendar because its winter and spring breaks and year ending are coordinated with the college schedule.
Check WCSD's calendar hub after weather or emergency closures because any activated make-up plan may revise a published PDF.

livingHere.intro: WCSD's service area combines a major high-desert metro with mountain and remote communities, which helps explain why one district publishes multiple student calendars.

highlights.label: Reno-Sparks
highlights.detail: The district's largest population center and the main reference point for the Balanced Calendar.

highlights.label: Incline Village
highlights.detail: Lake Tahoe schools use a separate Incline calendar with its own opening, local break, and ending pattern.

highlights.label: Gerlach
highlights.detail: The remote northern community uses a shorter, locally structured Gerlach calendar rather than the Balanced schedule.

highlights.label: TMCC High School
highlights.detail: Its calendar tracks college-class milestones as well as WCSD student dates.

districtFaqs.q: Which WCSD calendar should my student use?
districtFaqs.a: Most families should begin with the Balanced Calendar, but students at schools assigned to the Gerlach, Incline, or TMCC calendars must use that separate PDF. Confirm the track with the school before relying on a districtwide date.

districtFaqs.q: Are WCSD contingency days guaranteed days off?
districtFaqs.a: No. In the reviewed 2026-27 and 2027-28 Balanced Calendars, the final contingency dates are explicitly marked in session and lead to the last day of school. The 2025-26 calendar instead lists contingency dates after the last scheduled student day.

districtFaqs.q: Why does WCSD count some no-student professional-development days?
districtFaqs.a: The official PDFs note that designated professional-development dates are non-student days but count as school days in session under the cited Nevada Administrative Code provision.

districtFaqs.q: Does TMCC High School follow the Balanced Calendar?
districtFaqs.a: No. WCSD publishes a separate TMCC calendar that includes college-class start and end dates and different break and year-ending patterns.

districtFaqs.q: Are WCSD conference weeks full no-school weeks?
districtFaqs.a: Not necessarily. The Balanced PDFs identify conference weeks but do not label every conference-week date as a districtwide closure. Families should use school communications for appointment and dismissal details.

customSections.label: Which WCSD Calendar Applies?
customSections.content: This site uses the Balanced Calendar for its main date list. The separate calendars matter because their breaks, grading periods, contingency windows, and last days can differ.
